subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevents the sandbox container command from execing?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but every compatibility fix changes a sandbox hardening boundary or decides that affected Docker hosts are unsupported, which requires maintainer security intent.

options.title: Add Explicit Dangerous Opt-Out
options.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

options.title: Improve Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` unconditional and surface a precise startup/session/doctor error that explains the host incompatibility and supported mitigations.

options.title: Declare Host Unsupported
options.body: Document that Docker hosts rejecting `no-new-privileges` are unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Dangerous Opt-Out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on sandbox dangerous overrides, security reporting, and Docker config patterns that this decision would extend.
